evidence.text: Numerical landscapes usually set Λ_i=Λ, f_α=f and C=0, draw integer coefficients with |n_iα|≤3 and random relative phases, and repeatedly search for minima from random initial positions until the found-minimum distribution converges. Alignment-selected examples require R<10^−2.

destination.summary: Keeps low-VEV invisible axions separate from below-QCD breaking with a GeV-scale axion and from historical mixing proposals.

systems: Residual-discrete PQ models with low scalar VEVs
targets: Suppressed fermion couplings or altered axion mass regimes
Reduced high-scale tuning or gravity sensitivity
regimes: PQ breaking below QCD with GeV-scale axion masses
assumptions: Experimental viability is model- and source-date-specific
The historical mixing proposal supplies no established viable premise
conventions: Small scalar VEVs need not imply the same decay constant or coupling pattern
Low-VEV invisible and low-decay-constant heavy axions are distinct
includes: Regime comparisons with ordinary invisible-axion assumptions
excludes: A current certification that all experimental limits are evaded
An inferred dark-matter role for the supplied GeV-scale model

sources.title: Peccei-Quinn symmetry with residual symmetries

evidence.text: Can a PQ symmetry with residual discrete subgroups produce an invisible axion from low, potentially TeV-scale scalar VEVs, suppressing its fermion couplings while avoiding the Higgs-portal tuning associated with a very high symmetry-breaking scale?

sources.title: Axion from pseudo Goldstone seesaw without Peccei-Quinn symmetry

evidence.text: The historical manuscript asks whether tiny mixing between heavy and ultralight pseudo-Goldstone bosons could produce an axion without an anomalous Peccei–Quinn global symmetry, while keeping symmetry-breaking scales near TeV.

sources.title: GeV-scale QCD Axion

evidence.text: Can Peccei–Quinn breaking below the QCD scale solve strong CP while allowing a GeV-scale axion, avoiding existing constraints and producing observable hadronic or ultraviolet-completion signatures?

sources.title: Peccei-Quinn symmetry with residual symmetries

evidence.text: In the DFSZ construction, remove the three Goldstone modes eaten by W± and Z, identify the remaining axion direction, and project its couplings onto SM quark axial currents. Higgs-portal effects are estimated by inserting singlet VEVs into the scalar potential.

sources.title: Axion from pseudo Goldstone seesaw without Peccei-Quinn symmetry

evidence.text: Removes scalar phases from fermion masses by chiral field redefinitions, integrates derivative-current terms by parts, and invokes the axial triangle anomaly to infer gluon and photon couplings. These are manuscript calculations around its assumed vacuum.

sources.title: GeV-scale QCD Axion

evidence.text: Heavy-quark matching and running estimate κ at the QCD scale. Mixing with the vector-like quark is used to estimate weak-current shifts, while the dimension-five operator determines a three-body Higgs decay width.

sources.title: Peccei-Quinn symmetry with residual symmetries

evidence.text: Project the fermion-coupled phase P1 onto the normalized Goldstone direction, then use the fermion Dirac equation to express its interaction through an axial-current derivative. The small P1 overlap produces a large effective axion decay constant.

sources.title: Peccei-Quinn symmetry with residual symmetries

evidence.text: Minimize the scalar potential using ∂V/∂vi = 0 and analyze the pseudoscalar mass matrix. Breaking one global U(1) leaves one massless Goldstone direction and n − 1 massive pseudoscalars; the general massive eigenstates are deliberately not displayed.

sources.title: Axion from pseudo Goldstone seesaw without Peccei-Quinn symmetry

evidence.text: Integrates out Δ and Ω to obtain effective scalar operators, parametrizes the four light scalars by radial fields and phases, and expands the phase-dependent potential around assumed VEVs. Orthogonal transformations separate eaten modes from a two-field pseudo-Goldstone mass matrix.
